what_its_for: Teprotumumab-trbw is used to treat thyroid eye disease (also called Graves' eye disease). This is a condition where the muscles and tissues behind your eyes become swollen, causing your eyes to bulge, feel painful, or have double vision. This medicine helps reduce that swelling and can improve how your eyes look and feel.
how_to_take: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) directly into your vein by a healthcare provider in a clinic or infusion center. You cannot give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 60 to 90 minutes. You will receive a total of 8 infusions, given once every 3 weeks.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your body weight. The first infusion is usually given at a lower dose, and then the dose is increased for the remaining 7 infusions. All doses are given once every 3 weeks for a total of 8 treatments over about 5 to 6 months.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion appointment, call your doctor or infusion center as soon as possible. Try to reschedule within a reasonable time frame so your treatment stays on track. Do not try to skip doses, as completing all 8 infusions is important for the medicine to work properly.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. It is prepared and stored by healthcare professionals at the infusion center or pharmacy. If you have any questions about storage, ask your healthcare team.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, because this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Avoid becoming pregnant during this time. Also let your doctor know about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some may interact with this treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience any of the following: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; increased thirst or urination (signs of high blood sugar); muscle cramps or spasms; hearing loss or ringing in the ears; shortness of breath or chest tightness during or after the infusion; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; rash or hives; vision changes; or any signs of an allergic reaction. Also tell your doctor if you have diabetes or inflammatory bowel disease, as this medicine may make those conditions worse.
when_it_works: Many patients start to notice improvement in eye bulging, swelling, and double vision after just a few infusions. The full benefit of treatment is usually seen by the time you complete all 8 infusions or within a few months after finishing. Some patients continue to improve even after their last dose. Talk to your doctor about what results to expect for your specific situation.
special_populations: Pregnant women should not use this medicine because it can cause serious harm to the baby, including hearing problems. Women who can become pregnant must use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last infusion. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. If you have diabetes, your blood sugar levels may increase during treatment and will need to be monitored closely. If you have inflammatory bowel disease (such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis), this medicine may cause a flare-up, so your doctor should monitor you carefully. Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established.
